steps.question: In the 12-sample (6 treated vs 6 control) kidney Salmon gene-count matrix, do the two PCA-visible clusters of six samples align with treatment condition, or do they cross condition roughly 3v3, indicating an unrecorded technical/biological batch orthogonal to treatment?
acceptance_criteria: Counts (12000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata (12 x 2) are loaded and sample IDs are matched between files
Low-count genes are filtered (e.g. CPM-based filter) before normalization
A DESeq2 or equivalent size-factor normalization (e.g. rlog/vst) is applied and PCA is recomputed to confirm the two six-sample clusters reported in the data context

A contingency table of PCA-cluster membership x treatment condition is produced and a Fisher's exact test or equivalent is reported to quantify whether the split is confounded with treatment or crosses it
A binary cluster label (surrogate batch) per sample is written out for use by the DE step
Report explicitly states whether the design is estimable (i.e., cluster is not perfectly collinear with condition) before any DE model is proposed

steps.context: Building on the cluster-vs-condition characterization in T1S1. steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control kidney samples when the model includes the PCA-derived surrogate cluster covariate (or an SVA-estimated surrogate variable) alongside condition, compared to a naive condition-only model?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 is run with design ~ cluster + condition (or ~ SV1 + condition if SVA is used) on the filtered/normalized counts from T1S1, contingent on T1S1 confirming the design is estimable

The two DE gene lists (adjusted vs naive) are compared explicitly (overlap count, genes gained/lost) so the effect of the batch adjustment on the DE call set is transparent

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with hidden batch adjustment
plan.analytical_narrative: The data context reports a PCA where 12 kidney samples (6 treated, 6 control) split into two clusters of six that do NOT follow condition, with no recorded processing batch. This is the classic signature of an unrecorded technical batch (or a confound like sex, sample source, or processing date) that is orthogonal to or crossed with treatment. Running a naive two-group DESeq2 model without accounting for this structure risks either (a) the batch dominating the DE result if it happens to correlate with condition, or (b) inflated residual variance masking true treatment effects if it does not. The plan first characterizes the cluster structure quantitatively (does the 6/6 PCA split correspond to a balanced 3v3 crossing of treatment, or does it align with treatment itself, which would mean confounding rather than a correctable batch), then treats the surrogate cluster label as a latent batch by including it (or an SVA-estimated surrogate variable) as a covariate in the differential expression model. Results are compared with and without batch adjustment to make the impact of this decision transparent, followed by pathway enrichment on the batch-adjusted gene list using the human WikiPathways reference held in this environment.
